reconcile.connective: The strongest defence does not harmonize the wording but rejects it: the Eliphaz-line "duke Korah" of 36:16 is a scribal interpolation, absent from the Samaritan Pentateuch.

discrepancy.connective: Steve Wells's Skeptic's Annotated Bible presses the row, noting Korah is named Esau's son in 36:5/14/18 yet a grandson via Eliphaz in 36:15-16, and that the "two Korahs" reply fails because no Korah is listed among Eliphaz's sons.

excerpts.excerpt_text: It is also certain, from Gen 36:5, Gen 36:14, that Korah was the son of Esau (not of Eliphaz) by Aholibamah; and as such he is properly mentioned in Gen 36:18: These are the sons of Aholibamah, Esau's wife: duke Jeush, duke Jaalam, Duke Korah. It is clear, therefore, that some transcriber has improperly inserted duke Korah in Gen 36:16; from which interpolation both the Samaritan text and the Samaritan version are free.
excerpts.on_tension_rationale: Directly resolves the son-vs-grandson tension by attributing Korah's appearance in the Eliphaz line (36:16) to a copyist's interpolation that the Samaritan text lacks; the verbatim Kennicott quotation Clarke endorses. French-spaced ' :' before 'These' normalized to ':'; full sentences end on real source periods (no truncation marker).
